title: Housing funding, parking structure and sanctioned encampment update
subtitle: Also covered: Rapid Housing Initiative, accessibility committee appointments, land purchases, symphony funding request, COVID update, provincial funding letter.
overview: Regional Council approved steps to expand affordable housing. It authorized staff to take part in Round 3 of the federal Rapid Housing Initiative and to issue an 18-month conditional commitment to transfer 34 Peel Street in New Hamburg to a non-profit housing developer {{vote:m9}}. Council also extended its option to buy a share of the City of Waterloo parking structure to June 30, 2023 {{vote:m5}}.

Council approved two land purchases from the Province of Ontario, appointed eight members to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee, accepted transit funding under the Safe Restart Agreement, and wrote off $169,481.50 in uncollectable receivables {{vote:m7}}. Before the vote, the meeting held a closed session, and the minutes report no decisions from it.

Staff said the sanctioned encampment on Erb Street will not open in February as hoped. They now target mid to late March, and a community meeting was set for January 26. Delegations from the Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony and a food waste technology company were referred to staff or to a February 7 report. Public Health also updated Council on COVID-19 and respiratory illness.

decisions.item: Affordable housing and Rapid Housing Initiative
decisions.detail: Council continued its support for affordable housing at 34 Peel Street, New Hamburg, authorized a conditional commitment letter valid for 18 months, and authorized staff to enter and deliver Rapid Housing Initiative Round 3 agreements and projects {{vote:m9}}.
Council extended the option to purchase a share of the City of Waterloo parking structure to June 30, 2023 and authorized senior staff to execute the final option agreement {{vote:m5}}.
Council approved two agreements of purchase and sale with the Province of Ontario for parts of a property in Waterloo, at $394,500 and $84,750 plus taxes {{vote:m10}}.

Council appointed seven named new members and an agency representative from the Brain Injury Association Waterloo Wellington to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee for a term ending December 31, 2026 {{vote:m8}}.

decisions.item: Transit funding agreement and receivables write-off
decisions.detail: Council authorized a Transfer Payment Agreement with the Province for Safe Restart Agreement Transit Stream Phase 4 and wrote off $169,481.50 in 2022 accounts receivable {{vote:m7}}.

debate: On the provincial funding letter, one councillor said it did not explain why Toronto received deficit support, and noted that the Region would be compensated only if it exceeds housing pledge and growth targets. Another councillor called that condition concerning and new, and said it needs clarification.
The Chair said the province has promised to keep municipalities whole but no one has defined what that means. The Chair suggested following up with local MPPs.

On the Erb Street encampment, staff took responsibility for announcing a February date too early. Staff said the community space needed redesign and Canadian Standards Association approval, and that rushing would be risky.

Councillors urged speed because larger encampments remain in winter. Others said no apology was needed given the project's complexity. One asked whether the design could be reused in Cambridge, and staff said another site may be needed once lessons are learned.

The food waste delegate said a household unit can serve multi-residential buildings, and councillors asked about distribution, resident cost and prior contact with staff. Staff agreed to talk with the company, noting that provincial organics policy focuses on multi-residential buildings.
